title: Openness of purity for a flat finitely presented family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], flat over $S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then $\{s\in S:F\text{ is pure along }X_s\}$ is open in $S$, where purity along a fibre is [def-sfb-scheme-relative-purity]. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $S$.

proof.text: Fix $s$ in the asserted purity locus $U$. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-fibre-projective-etale-cover] to obtain $e:(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})\to(S,s)$, affine $X^{\prime},S^{\prime}$, and $g,p$ with $fg=ep$, $g$ etale, $X_s\subseteq g(X^{\prime})$, and $N=\Gamma(X^{\prime},g^*F)$ projective over $A=\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$. Its flatness hypothesis holds on the entire fibre because $F$ is flat over $S$. Write $G=g^*F$, $Y=X\times_SS^{\prime}$, $F_Y=\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, $q:Y\to S^{\prime}$ and $h=(g,p):X^{\prime}\to Y$.

The module $G$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented by pullback permanence. Since $g$ and $e$ are etale they are locally of finite presentation. The composite $fg=ep$ is locally of finite presentation, and the over-base permanence lemma applied to $ep$ and $e$ gives that $p$ is locally of finite presentation. Both its schemes are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so $p$ is finitely presented. Projectivity of $N$ makes it flat over $A$, and the affine-chart flatness criterion makes $G$ flat over $S^{\prime}$. Therefore the projectivity-implies-universal-purity direction of [lem-sfb-affine-flat-fp-projectivity-purity] applies to $p,G$: $G$ is universally pure over $S^{\prime}$, in particular pure along every fibre.

The projection $Y\to X$ is etale by base change of $e$, so cancellation with $g$ makes $h$ etale. Hence its image $W=h(X^{\prime})$ is open in $Y$. It is quasi-compact over $S^{\prime}$: for any affine open $B\subseteq S^{\prime}$, $W\cap q^{-1}(B)$ is the continuous image under $h$ of $p^{-1}(B)$, which is quasi-compact because $p$ is finitely presented. Base change makes $q$ finitely presented, and $F_Y$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented. Thus [lem-sfb-scheme-assassin-open-constructible] applies over the affine base $S^{\prime}$ and shows that $E=\{t\in S^{\prime}:\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_t}((F_Y)_t)\subseteq W_t\}$ is constructible.

Apply [lem-sfb-purity-etale-assassin-criterion] to the original diagram at $s$. Its source $p$ is of finite type, $G$ is pure along $X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}$, $F$ is flat along $X_s$, and $g(X^{\prime})$ contains the whole fibre, hence its associated points. Since $s\in U$, the criterion says that $W$ contains all points of the relative assassin of $F_Y$ lying over generalizations of $s^{\prime}$. The relative assassin is the union of the fibrewise associated points by [def-trf-relative-assassin]; hence every generalization of $s^{\prime}$ belongs to $E$.

The affine scheme $S^{\prime}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence spectral. The complement $C=S^{\prime}\setminus E$ is constructible. If $s^{\prime}\in\overline C$, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization], applied to the one-member family $C$, would give $c\in C$ specializing to $s^{\prime}$, contradicting the preceding step. Consequently $V=S^{\prime}\setminus\overline C$ is an open neighbourhood of $s^{\prime}$ contained in $E$. This proves the needed Tag 05LW neighbourhood conclusion directly from existing spectral-space lemmas.

For $t\in V$, apply [lem-sfb-purity-etale-assassin-criterion] over $S^{\prime}$ to $q:Y\to S^{\prime}$, $F_Y$, the identity elementary neighbourhood $(S^{\prime},t)$, and $h:X^{\prime}\to Y$. The pullback-composition isomorphism identifies $h^*F_Y$ with $G$, since $\operatorname{pr}_Xh=g$. The sheaf $F_Y$ is flat over $S^{\prime}$ by relatively flat base change. The other hypotheses hold by steps 2 and 3, and $t\in E$ gives the required containment of the associated points of the fibre in $h(X^{\prime})$. Every generalization $u$ of $t$ lies in the open $V$, hence in $E$; thus all relative associated points over these $u$ lie in $W=h(X^{\prime})$. The reverse implication of the criterion proves that $F_Y$ is pure along $Y_t$.

For any $s_1\in e(V)$ choose $t\in V$ mapping to $s_1$. The etale map $e$ is flat at $t$. Apply [lem-sfb-purity-flat-point-descent] to the purity of $F_Y$ along $Y_t$ just proved: $F$ is pure along $X_{s_1}$, so $e(V)\subseteq U$. The image $e(V)$ is open by etale openness and contains $s$. Every $s\in U$ therefore has an open neighbourhood contained in $U$, proving the assertion.

Item statement unchanged; there is no re-split note. All seven steps check against the cited statements. Steps 1–2: the 05KW chart, finite presentation of p via 01TR and 02FV, and flatness of G via the affine-chart criterion; then the projective⇒universally pure direction of the 05MD node. Step 3: h is étale, W is open and quasi-compact over S′ because q∘h=p, and the 05KR node makes E constructible. Step 4: the 05L4 forward direction plus the union definition of Ass puts every generalization of s′ in E. Step 5: the 05LW argument from spectral spaces and Topology 0903 on C=S′∖E. Steps 6–7: 05L4 again over (S′,t) with the identity neighbourhood, then 05J9(1) descent at a point where e is flat. This correctly fixes the source, which does not check that (S′,t) is elementary over (S,e(t)). No cycle: 05MD's proof does not use 05MC. The three new nodes match their sources hypothesis by hypothesis and are statement-only with correct stmt_deps. They are not duplicates: the 05ID and 05ME nodes are pointwise and the 05ME node cites the item. Tested on F=0, the identity base change and a field base. Batch-5 check: def-trf-relative-assassin is the general definition of associated points (02OJ/05AT). lem-sfb-scheme-assassin-open-constructible reaches the trace-formula chapter only through that definition. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so both are accepted. No SGA citation.
